'''Jakob Rosanes''' (also '''Jacob'''; 16 August 1842 – 6 January 1922) was a [[German people|German]] [[mathematician]] who worked on [[algebraic geometry]] and [[invariant theory]]. He was also a [[chess master]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jakob Rosanes - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Rosanes/ |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
[[File:Grab Jakob Rosanes.jpg|thumb|Grave of Jacob Rosanes at the Old Jewish Cemetery in Breslau]]
Rosanes was a grandson of Rabbi [[Akiva Eiger]], one of the most revered Jewish religious scholars of the [[Talmud]] and ''halachic'' decisors of the 18th century. Eiger's daughter Baila was Rosanes' mother. Rosanes grew up during a period when the [[Age of Enlightenment|Enlightenment]] and increasing opportunities for social, academic and economic advancement for culturally assimilated Jews influenced large numbers of Jews to reconsider their faith. He was not religiously observant, and his children converted to [[Christianity]]. 

Rosanes studied at [[University of Berlin]] and the [[University of Breslau]]. He obtained his [[doctorate]] from Breslau ([[Wrocław]]) in 1865 and taught there for the rest of his working life. He became [[professor]] in 1876 and [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the university during the years 1903–1904.<ref>[http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/view.jsp?letter=R&artid=363 Rosanes, Jacob — Jewish Encyclopedia]</ref> In his ‘inspiring’ rectorial speech on 15 October 1903, he described the development of mathematics in the nineteenth century.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rektoratsreden im 19. und 20. Jahrhundert – Online-Bibliographie - Jakob Rosanes |url=https://www.historische-kommission-muenchen-editionen.de/rektoratsreden/anzeige/index.php?type=rektor&id=-2072720413 |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=www.historische-kommission-muenchen-editionen.de}}</ref>

Rosanes made significant contributions in [[Cremona group|Cremona transformation]]s.

== Notable chess games ==
* [http://www.chessgames.com/perl/chessgame?gid=1019149 Jakob Rosanes vs Adolf Anderssen, Breslau 1862, Spanish Game: Berlin Defense. Rio Gambit Accepted (C67), 1-0] Sometimes, Rosanes was able to beat even one of the best masters of his time, [[Adolf Anderssen]]...  
* [http://www.chessgames.com/perl/chessgame?gid=1019162 Jakob Rosanes vs Adolf Anderssen, Breslau, 1863, King's Gambit: Accepted. Kieseritzky Gambit Anderssen Defense (C39), 0-1] ...but as shows this beautiful game, the opposite result was probably quite usual in their games.
